counterexample: Tick spacing 10. Positions [50, 100) and [100, 150), each with liquidity L. Tick 100 is initialized but its net liquidity is 0 (+L from one position, -L from the other). Start 100, end 40. The walk returns [50]; it should return [100, 50]. The liquidity total still comes out right in this case, but an initialized tick inside the walk is dropped. The hook therefore never adds the reward growth earned above tick 100 to rewardGrowthOutsideX128[100], so the position [50, 100) collects rewards earned by the position [100, 150).
summary: When the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and its net liquidity, read from the pool manager, is not zero, sets the current tick to the start plus one inside an unchecked block so the search includes it. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.
